source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting excessive industrial emissions in an air-quality report

1. Start with the monitoring records.
2.
completion:
Document all equipment used in data collection and calibration methods.
3. List monitoring dates and times.
4. Provide weather conditions during the monitoring period.
5. Categorize emissions data based on specific pollutants (e.g., SO2, NOx, CO, particulates, VOCs).
6. Use established standards and units for reporting quantities (e.g., tons/year, mg/Nm³).
7. Record the operation status of the facility (e.g., production levels, shutdown periods).
8. Include photographic and video evidence if available.
9. Detail any observed anomalies or spikes in emission levels.
10. Compare observed emissions to permissible emission limits provided by local, state, or national regulations.
11. Include relevant engineering calculations for emissions (e.g., mass balance, emission factors).
12. Identify the potential sources of excessive emissions within the facility.
13. Document any pollution control technologies or mitigation measures in place.
14. Outline the compliance status with environmental
